highlights: The distillery segment was the primary growth driver, achieving its highest-ever production and sales volumes (alcohol production +18.2% YoY to 236,510 KL), benefiting from lower maize procurement costs and improved feedstock availability; distillery annual revenue (net of excise) reached ₹1,550 crore.

Sugarcane crushing declined 8.8% to 8.25 million tonnes in the 2025-26 season due to lower yields in western UP and cane diversion toward alternative sweeteners, though improved recovery kept sugar production roughly flat at 0.91 million tonnes.
Q4 FY26 net profit declined 10.5% YoY to ₹167.4 crore, pressured by elevated sugarcane procurement costs and weaker Power Transmission Business profitability/deferred deliveries.
TRIVENI.outlook: Major corporate restructuring completed: the Composite Scheme of Arrangement became effective May 19, 2026 — Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL) was amalgamated into Triveni, and the Power Transmission Business is being demerged into a new entity, Triveni Power Transmission Limited (TPTL), effective April 1, 2026 (accounting impact reflected in FY27). TPTL is expected to list independently by end of August 2026. ICRA upgraded the company's long-term credit rating to AA+ Stable, removing it from "under-watch" status. Promoters disclosed zero share encumbrance for FY26, a clean governance signal.

highlights: Full-year PBT fell 38.7% YoY to ₹30.48 crore from ₹49.69 crore, driven by cost of materials consumed rising 16.4% YoY to ₹80.87 crore even as revenue declined 2.6% — a clear margin-squeeze pattern.

Q4 FY26 standalone net profit fell 40.3% YoY to ₹7.46 crore (per one source) / consolidated PAT of ₹5.09 crore (down 60.51% YoY per another source) — exact figures vary by standalone/consolidated basis across reporting sources, but the directional decline is consistent.
Employee costs surged disproportionately (24–33% YoY increases reported across different quarters) even as revenue declined, indicating adverse operating leverage.
WENDT.outlook: Operating margins have compressed sharply and repeatedly through FY26 — from 22.76% to 11.81% in Q2, and from 24.49% to 16.35% in Q4 — reflecting sustained demand softness in core industrial tooling and abrasives markets, not a single-quarter event. Board recommended a final dividend of ₹10 per share, taking the total FY26 dividend to ₹30 per share (consistent with the company's historical ~25% payout ratio). A CEO resignation in September 2025 and a ₹94,400 fine for a 34-day board-structure non-compliance were also disclosed during the year — minor governance items worth noting, though not characterised as major issues.

highlights: Margin compression was a persistent theme across nearly every quarter of FY26: Q2 gross margin fell to 5.01% from 10.88% YoY; Q3 net profit fell 59.73% YoY despite 21.72% revenue growth; interest costs surged 86.10% YoY in Q3 to ₹9.77 crore.
Operating cash flow turned sharply negative (-₹80.52 crore) in FY25, with continued working capital stress flagged through FY26 (debtors turnover ratio fell to a record-low 2.64x in H1).
Board recommended a final dividend of ₹2 per share, with the Promoter and Promoter Group waiving their right to receive it — a notable signal amid the ongoing corporate restructuring.
LUXIND.outlook: Major corporate development: the board approved a three-way demerger of the business following a Family Settlement Agreement (FSA) among the Todi family branches, intended to give different family members clear control over separate entities and improve operational focus/efficiency. Minority shareholders will receive one share in each of the new entities for every Lux Industries share held. As an initial step, Lux Industries incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, "Lux and Cozi Limited," in West Bengal (May 22, 2026) to house the proposed demerger of "Vertical A" — its board includes promoter Ashok Kumar Todi and Executive Director Saket Todi. Independent analysts have flagged execution risk and valuation uncertainty stemming from this complex family-led split, alongside concern that the current premium valuation (P/E ~45–49x) versus peer Dollar Industries (P/E ~13–25x) is hard to justify given the deteriorating margin and return-ratio trajectory.

MOLDTKPAC.outlook: Consolidation of 5 Hyderabad manufacturing units into 2 is expected to deliver full efficiency benefits from FY27 onward, per management commentary. The company is pursuing a strategic MoU with Vibe Generation Holdings (UK) for IP-led, high-precision safety closures, targeting a USD 1 billion global market opportunity with revenue potential of USD 25-30 million (₹250 crore) over five years. Board recommended a final dividend of ₹2.70 per share (27%), in addition to an interim dividend of ₹2.00 per share (40%) already paid; the company received an income tax demand notice of ₹4.84 crore for AY 2022-23 during the year.

highlights: Export revenue reached a record ₹971 crore for FY26 (+37.7% YoY), now accounting for ~59% of total revenue — a near-fourfold increase from ₹268 crore in FY22, reflecting a structural shift in the company's revenue mix.
LNG segment posted its best-ever annual revenue at ₹457 crore, nearly doubling YoY, while transport tank/semi-trailer annual sales crossed 300 units for the first time in company history.

Q4 FY26 alone delivered record quarterly revenue of ₹475 crore (+24.2% YoY), with a ₹200 crore order from a major US private aerospace company — management noted this was awarded "based on performance of earlier orders," signalling a moving-up-the-value-chain trajectory rather than a one-off win.
INOXCVA.outlook: Order backlog stood at ₹1,514 crore at FY26-end (63% export orders), with roughly ₹1,200 crore executable in FY27 — meaning nearly 75% of FY26 revenue is already locked in before any new order is won. Despite 19.3% PAT growth, cash flow from operations actually slipped from ₹122 crore in FY25 to ₹117 crore in FY26, as large turnkey projects bill on milestone-based terms requiring the company to fund work-in-progress — a working capital dynamic independent analysts are watching closely. Secured the first marine LNG fuel tank order from Cochin Shipyard (6 tanks of 800 cubic metres each) for LNG-powered vessels, and beverage keg approvals now span Heineken, AB InBev, and Molson Coors — together representing over 40% of the global beer market.
